name: FastVideo FastH3 — video with sound, from a first and/or last frame (8 steps)
description:
Write a scene and get a short film back with its own soundtrack — and optionally pin how it starts, how it ends, or both.

Give a FIRST frame and the clip begins there. Give a LAST frame and it arrives there. Give both and the model travels between them, which is the way to animate between two stills. Give neither and it is plain text-to-video. A slot you leave empty is removed from the graph, so it cannot influence the result.

★ Pick the shape that matches your first frame. The model stretches the first frame to fill the video, so a portrait picture in a widescreen video comes out squashed. The LAST frame is treated differently — it is cropped to fit rather than stretched, so its shape matters less.

Write the prompt the way this model expects: bind the picture to the timeline first, then describe the shot. The default prompt shows the form —
"For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced." followed by "integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] …".

Then describe camera, action and sound in that one block. Naming the audio ("we hear rain on metal, a distant siren") is what earns a deliberate soundtrack rather than an invented one. With no frames at all you can drop the binding line and write the description alone.

This is MiniMax H3 distilled by FastVideo to 8 sampling steps, so it is several times quicker than the full model. Multi-reference conditioning was not distilled — for that use the base MiniMax H3 bundles.

promptGuides.label: MiniMax H3 — official video prompt guide
promptGuides.tip: Bind the picture to a time first ("at 0.00 seconds … <Picture 1> is fully referenced"), then write one block covering framing, camera move, action and the sound.

promptGuides.label: FastVideo FastH3 8-Step V2 — the distilled checkpoint
